## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs fixing before merge: it stores keys without lower-casing them, so `get` can't find any entry written under a mixed-case key.

## Changes
The pull request raises `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 and updates the comment to match. It also adds a `Cache.set` method, plus tests for a set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1); c.get("alpha")` returns `None`, because `set` writes `self._store[key]` while `get` reads `key.lower()`. This breaks the rule at `app/cache.py:14`: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` only sets the already-lowercase `"alpha"`, so it can't catch this. — Callers that set mixed-case keys get silent cache misses, and those entries are never evicted by `get`, so the store keeps growing. — Fix: use `self._store[key.lower()] = ...`, and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` to set a mixed-case key.
